evidence.detail: HEAD and launcher target both resolve to f211f62ab4d941ba53f77d1d02e6e9819596de44; base resolves to e94ef5abad6e95ec899a7bca04e30e9dc3dbea81. Worktree was clean and detached at the target.
The exact base-to-target diff contains 11 changed files: analyzer.py, rules.py, server.py, analyzer/server tests and fixtures, plus workflow records.
Independent test execution ran 62 tests: 47 passed and 15 server tests errored because the review sandbox denied loopback socket binding. Exit status was 1.
Independent compilation could not complete because the read-only sandbox denied creation of __pycache__. Exit status was 1.
Governance validation could not complete because no writable temporary directory was available in the review sandbox. Exit status was 1.
The committed handoff claims compile exit 0, 62 passing tests, and governance validation passing, but those results could not be independently reproduced in this read-only execution environment.

evidence: Expected: acceptance criterion 6 and the issue scope require every rule to declare required data-contract fields and become not evaluable when required evidence is absent.
Observed: Rule.requires is metadata only. analyzer.analyze calls rule.check directly and never validates required fields. Most checks convert absent fields to empty values and return FAIL.
The incomplete fixture is an empty policy list and its test asserts not-evaluable status for only two rules; the remaining rules produce failures despite having no evidence.
graph.normalize_policy also converts absent or malformed fields to empty defaults, so the analyzer cannot distinguish missing evidence from known-empty evidence.
findings.remediation: Preserve field-presence/evidence metadata in the normalized contract or define another reliable completeness signal, enforce each rule's requires declaration before evaluation, and expand the incomplete fixture/tests to prove every affected rule is excluded rather than failed.
findings.title: Required-field metadata does not control evaluability
findings.verification: Analyze policies missing each declared requirement and assert the corresponding rule is not_evaluable, contributes no finding, and is excluded from both score numerator and denominator.

evidence: Expected: ISSUE-0004 explicitly includes a starter rule for an overly broad all-users plus all-apps grant.
Observed: rules.RULES contains nine rules, but none evaluates the combination of conditions.includeUsers, conditions.includeApplications, and grant controls for excessive breadth.
The strong and weak fixture tests contain no assertion for this required rule.
findings.remediation: Add the required declarative overly-broad-grant rule with documented weight, severity, required fields, rationale and remediation, plus positive, negative and missing-evidence fixture coverage.
findings.title: Required overly broad grant rule is absent
findings.verification: Run fixture tests showing an unsafe all-users/all-apps grant produces the expected finding, a safely scoped policy does not, and absent required evidence is not evaluable.

evidence: Expected: the ISSUE-0003 contract defines local user-supplied break_glass_ids input for ISSUE-0004 to consume.

Observed: analyzer.analyze accepts the input, but server._analysis always invokes analyzer.analyze(policies) without any input source. Consequently the live /api/analysis path can never evaluate the break-glass rule.
The endpoint tests exercise only the permanently absent-input path.
findings.remediation: Provide an approved local input path for sanitized break-glass IDs, retain the values in memory only, pass them into analyzer.analyze, and test supplied, absent, invalid and cleared input behavior.
findings.title: API analysis cannot consume the break-glass input contract
findings.verification: Exercise /api/analysis with a supplied valid emergency-account ID and assert the rule passes or fails as appropriate; assert absent/invalid input remains not evaluable and no input is persisted.

evidence: Expected: emergency accounts should be excluded from all applicable broad MFA/block policies, as stated by the rule remediation.
Observed: the check passes when any one broad policy excludes any supplied emergency ID. It does not require every supplied ID to be excluded, nor exclusion from every broad policy.
A tenant with two broad policies where only one excludes one of two emergency accounts is therefore reported as passing.
findings.remediation: Require every sanitized break-glass ID to be excluded from every applicable enabled broad lockout policy, or explicitly document and obtain approval for a weaker intended definition. Report the noncompliant policies/accounts without exposing unnecessary identifiers.
findings.title: Break-glass rule passes partial exclusions
findings.verification: Add tests with multiple broad policies and multiple emergency IDs; the rule must fail if any applicable policy omits any supplied emergency account and pass only when coverage is complete.

evidence: Expected: the issue documentation section requires README/verify instructions describing the offline analyzer test and explaining that the score is heuristic rather than compliance.
Observed: README.md was not changed in the candidate diff and still says analysis is not implemented yet.
The handoff documents the scoring formula, but it does not satisfy the requested user-facing README/verify update.
findings.remediation: Reconcile the issue's allowed paths with its documentation requirement, then update README/verify content to describe the implemented offline fixtures, deterministic test command, scoring formula/limitations, and non-compliance meaning.
findings.title: Required analyzer documentation is stale and missing
findings.verification: Inspect README/verify from the repaired candidate and run the documented offline command; confirm it no longer says analysis is unimplemented and clearly labels the score heuristic.

limitations: The mandatory test command could not be fully executed because the review sandbox prohibits loopback socket binding; 15 server integration tests errored for that environmental reason.
The mandatory compile command could not complete because the read-only checkout prohibits creation of Python bytecode caches.
Governance validation could not complete because the sandbox exposed no writable temporary directory.

The author-recorded successful checks are repository claims rather than independently reproducible evidence in this review. Per the binding, execution failure requires BLOCKED even though substantive required changes were also found.
No live Microsoft sign-in or Graph request was attempted; those are protected actions and are not issue-completion evidence.
review.summary: Target identity matches, but the review is blocked because mandatory checks could not be independently completed in the read-only sandbox. Static review also found five required changes: missing-evidence declarations are not enforced, the required overly-broad-grant rule is absent, the API cannot receive break-glass IDs, partial break-glass exclusions incorrectly pass, and required README/verify documentation remains stale.
